subject.title: fix(gateway): clients can identify authorization failures

question: Should authorization denials replace the existing top-level `INVALID_REQUEST` gateway code with `FORBIDDEN`, or should semantic authorization classification remain additive in `error.details` until a versioned protocol transition is approved?
rationale: Both approaches can expose actionable authorization information, but choosing the permanent public gateway error-code contract requires owner intent because existing third-party clients may branch on the current code.

options.title: Keep the top-level code stable
options.body: Retain `INVALID_REQUEST` for current clients and use the new discriminated `details` objects as the additive machine-readable authorization contract.

options.title: Approve a versioned error-code transition
options.body: Keep `FORBIDDEN`, but document the compatibility break, define the protocol/version rollout, and add downstream-client upgrade coverage.

options.title: Accept the immediate behavior change
options.body: Land the `FORBIDDEN` replacement as-is and explicitly accept that older code-based client handlers may need updates.

recommendation.title: Keep the top-level code stable
recommendation.body: Retain `INVALID_REQUEST` for current clients and use the new discriminated `details` objects as the additive machine-readable authorization contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only concrete gateway/protocol contact identified in the supplied review context; broader ownership history could not be established from the read-only inspection environment.
